children: won a U.S. Army contract worth up to $127 million to continue operating surveillance aircraft that gather intelligence for military commanders in Europe and other regions.

The award for the Airborne Reconnaissance and Targeting Exploitation Multi-Mission Intelligence System, or ARTEMIS, extends operations in the U.S. European Command area through summer 2027. The contract also includes two additional option years and allows the system to support missions in other regions.
has supported ARTEMIS operations since 2020. The system is designed to provide airborne intelligence collection and targeting information to military commanders.

ARTEMIS is based on a modified Bombardier Challenger 650 business jet equipped with military intelligence and sensing systems. Under the contractor-owned, contractor-operated arrangement, Leidos supplies the aircraft, mission systems, flight operations and support services.
The platform was initially deployed as a technology demonstrator but has since developed into a high-altitude ISR system capable of operating in multiple theaters.
The Army has used ARTEMIS as part of its effort to expand airborne intelligence capabilities while taking advantage of commercial aircraft that can be deployed relatively quickly.
The latest award was made through the Army's Common Hardware Systems-6, or CHS-6, contract vehicle.

CHS-6 is used by the Army, other U.S. military branches and federal agencies to acquire command, control, communications, computers, cyber, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance hardware and related services.
, the ARTEMIS award adds to its portfolio of airborne ISR, sensing and defense technology programs. The company has identified those areas as part of its NorthStar 2030 growth strategy.
